ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the lower left corner of the figure there is a cyano group labeled as NC, connected to a carbon chain containing an adjacent C-H; beside it is a negatively charged oxygen O−, a curved arrow points to this hydrogen, and another curved arrow shows the C-H bond electrons and adjacent electron density rearranging along the carbon chain toward the cyano group. Reasoning: update step by step according to the arrows; O− removes the shown H; the electron pair of the original C-H bond is used to form a new π bond; the adjacent π/electron density continues to migrate, making this lower-left fragment become a continuous multiple-bond system, and ending with the nitrile C#N. After updating the valences, the corresponding chain SMILES is C=C=C#N.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the relevant lower-left cyano-substituted fragment and the arrows indicating proton abstraction/electron relocation. Apply each curved arrow literally: remove the indicated H, use the C-H electron pair to form the new pi bond, and shift the adjacent pi/electron density so the carbon chain becomes a consecutive multiple-bond system terminating in the nitrile. After updating formal valences, write the final chain as C=C=C#N.
